The safest protocol uses a content-addressed Merkle-DAG where completed evidence is an ancestral node and reclamation only garbage-collects orphaned leaves; silent displacement is structurally impossible because overwriting a content-addressed hash changes its address.

Durably recorded: prepared root and post-crash audit attestation.

entries.claim: The safest protocol elevates a crash-without-terminal-record to a Byzantine fault scenario, requiring a Byzantine-fault-tolerant consensus among independent storage witnesses that the workspace contains no completed evidence before reclamation.
entries.qualification: Mechanism: treat workspace as potentially adversarial; reclamation proceeds only after BFT consensus among a quorum of storage nodes confirms no evidence-carrying object exists. Durably recorded: BFT-signed emptiness certificate.

entries.claim: The safest autonomous protocol is preserve-then-reclaim gated by a Byzantine quorum of signed null-attestations from an anti-entropy mesh, ensuring no completed evidence hash can be overlooked.
entries.qualification: Mechanism: seal workspace and broadcast reclamation intent to witness mesh; each node scans evidence namespace for problem fingerprint and returns positive hash or signed null-attestation. Reclamation permitted only upon BFT quorum of null-attestations. Durably recorded: reclamation intent, signed attestations, quorum threshold, final decision with monotonic epoch.

entries.claim: No autonomous reclamation protocol can guarantee never to silently displace completed evidence, because the absence of a terminal record is observationally equivalent to both incomplete execution and completed-but-lost execution; an external adjudicator must render the verdict.
entries.qualification: Mechanism: durably record deterministic checkpoint hashes of workspace at intervals and problem input specification; publish completed evidence to external namespace. After crash, quarantine workspace. External adjudicator compares checkpoint chain, evidence namespace, and problem input to render binding verdict. Reclamation permitted only upon adjudicator signature.

Silent displacement is structurally impossible if the workspace is replaced by a Merkle-DAG of pending side effects where completed evidence is defined as a content-addressed node replicated to a threshold of anchor nodes; reclamation is merely garbage collection of unreached leaves. The workspace is modeled as an append-only causal log of deterministic transformations, each yielding a content-addressed node. Evidence completion is the act of linking the evidence node to the problem trunk and achieving a threshold of anti-entropy anchors. The protocol durably records only the problem trunk root hash and the anchor node IDs. Crash recovery replays from the trunk root. Reclamation removes only orphan nodes that are not linked to any trunk, which by construction excludes all completed evidence.

The safest protocol is a consensus lease that treats workspace allocation as a distributed lock released only by publishing a completed evidence hash to a BFT ledger, and requires a signed absence certificate for reclamation after crash. Workspace allocation writes a lease record (workspace_id, problem_digest, epoch) to a BFT ledger. The holder must periodically renew. Completion appends the evidence hash and atomically releases the lease. If the process crashes without terminal record, the lease remains active. Reclamation requires a special absence certificate signed by a supermajority of consensus participants affirming they have not accepted an evidence hash for this lease epoch. The protocol durably records the lease entry, all renewal attempts, and the signed absence certificate.

If the workspace is strictly deterministic with respect to its inputs, the safety guarantee collapses to idempotency: the protocol must durably record the full entropy tape and external oracle log, making any displaced evidence recoverable by deterministic replay rather than preventing displacement. The workspace is a pure function of the problem input plus consumed entropy. The protocol durably records the problem input hash, a sequential log of all external random seeds and oracle responses, and intermediate Merkle checkpoints. Crash without terminal record triggers automatic deterministic replay from the last checkpoint. The scratch workspace can be safely reclaimed because evidence exists either in the durable intent log or is reconstructible. The safest protocol separates durability classes: an append-only intent log with strong durability for metadata, and a weakly durable scratch workspace. Reclamation is safe because evidence only exists upon pairing an intent record with a completion certificate in the durable log. Before computation, the process appends an intent record (problem_id, input_hash, lease_nonce) to a strongly durable, single-writer append-only log. The workspace itself is treated as weakly durable scratch. Upon completion, an immutable evidence artifact is written to a separate strongly durable store, and a completion certificate is appended to the intent log. The protocol durably records the intent log and all completion certificates.
